component.name: Alien
component.summary: Fan, lighting and performance control for Acer Predator laptops

description.p: Hardware control for Acer Predator systems on Linux, with no vendor software: fan modes and per-fan duty, four-zone keyboard lighting, guarded model-specific performance controls, and live temperature and fan telemetry.

An independent, from-scratch interoperability implementation of Acer's gaming WMI protocol, verified against real firmware. Where a control is accepted by the firmware but has no observable effect on a given model, Alien says so rather than implying it works.
On the reference machine, forcing the fans to maximum is worth roughly 48 percent more sustained CPU throughput, because the stock firmware fan curve holds the processor in thermal throttle.

This flatpak contains the desktop application only. The privileged helper it talks to, alien-daemon, must be installed on the host from a native package: it needs root and the acpi_call kernel module, which no sandbox can provide.

Adds the guarded PH315-53 OEM Normal, Faster and Turbo GPU modes, using exact P0 clock targets and ordered Acer firmware side effects with readback, rollback, explicit risk acknowledgement and manual-only notification-producing status reads.
Adds the canonical Alien application icon, exact PH315-53 lighting protocol, and advanced firmware controls.
First release: CLI, terminal UI and desktop application, with fan, lighting, performance and telemetry support.
